title: Payload Orchestra: consolidated failure conductor for request debugging
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Operators and engineers need to triage failed requests across models, regions, and routing policies quickly. Current console views are fragmented: separate failure lists, cost graphs, and payload inspectors require context switching. Goal: design a single, scannable Canvas — called Payload Orchestra — that surfaces correlated failed requests, retry histories, inferred error taxonomy, and per-request cost impact with one-click deep-inspection into payloads and KV cache state.

User scenarios: 
1) SRE during an outage wants to see whether a spike is infrastructure or model-related and identify the first failing request and subsequent retries.
2) Platform engineer investigating a regression wants to quickly correlate rollback/toggle events with model quality errors and cost spikes.
3) Support engineer needs to assemble a reproducible payload with exact headers, routing decision, and kvcache snapshot to attach to a ticket.

Scope: initial prototype for console-2026.04 will focus on hosted + dedicated telemetry (no private on-prem agent instrumentation yet), timeline+grouping UI, payload inspector modal, and an exportable debug bundle.

Out of scope: real-time streaming playback for high-throughput traces, advanced anomaly detection (future work).
acceptance_criteria: 1) A consolidated timeline view that shows failed requests, retries, routing fallbacks, and per-request cost (tokens+compute) aligned on a shared time axis; 2) Each timeline row expands to a payload inspector that shows request metadata, headers, model variant, KV cache diff snapshot, and the full request/response body; 3) Error taxonomy auto-tags each failure into one of five categories (Transient, Infrastructure, ModelQuality, Client, DegradedFallback) with color legend and manual override; 4) Filters (model, region, route, status, error category) and quick-presets (Last 15m, Last 6h, Canary-only) are available and persist per user; 5) Export debug bundle (.zip) that includes payload, retry trace, and cost breakdown for selected items; 6) Accessibility: keyboard navigation for opening the inspector ("p"), expanding a row (Enter), and copying debug bundle link (Cmd/Ctrl+K).
decisions: 1) Use a horizontal shared timeline as primary layout instead of stacked lists to make causal ordering obvious; 2) Error taxonomy names and color palette: Transient (blue), Infrastructure (red), ModelQuality (orange), Client (purple), DegradedFallback (amber); 3) Default grouping will be by request fingerprint (route+prompt-hash) with a secondary grouping by model variant; 4) Payload inspector will be a modal (not full route page) to minimize navigation; 5) Cost per-request will combine token cost + estimated compute cost (server-supplied) with a toggle to show token-only; 6) Manual taxonomy override writes an audit event to the debug bundle for future evals.
tradeoffs:
- Horizontal timeline improves causal reasoning but uses more horizontal real estate (requires responsive collapse behavior on small screens).
- Showing KV cache diffs may expose large arrays; initial implementation will show a sampled/trimmed diff with a link to fetch full snapshot on demand.
- Exporting debug bundles requires adding a backend aggregation endpoint (adds latency and infra work). This is scoped as async job with notification rather than inline generation.
- To keep initial scope small, private/on-prem agents are deferred to a later cycle, which means some enterprise customers won't get full KV snapshots immediately.
implementation_notes: Backend needs to expose aggregated trace objects: timestamp, request_id, parent_request_id, route, model_variant, token_count, token_cost, compute_estimate_usd, error_code, error_message, retry_index, kv_cache_digest (small), kv_cache_fetch_url (signed). Frontend should request paginated timeline windows and lazy-load payload inspector content via a signed API. Add audit event when a user overrides taxonomy. Use existing console trace palette for color consistency. Consider using continuous canvas library used by rollout timeline component to handle zooming/panning. Ensure feature flag (diagnostics.payload_orchestra) for staged rollout.
